entries.title: Smartphones and tablets: more than half of all computers aren't computers anymore
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2011 more than 50 percent of computing devices sold globally will not be PCs.
entries.metric: share of computing devices sold that are not PCs
entries.subject: Non-PC computing devices (smartphones, tablets)

entries.title: Operating system diversity: no standard emerges on the smartphone or tablet
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that by the end of 2011 no operating system on these devices will have a dominant market share.
entries.metric: dominant OS market share on smartphones and tablets
entries.subject: Mobile operating systems

entries.title: Tablets in the enterprise: more than just a toy
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2011 more than 25 percent of all tablet computers will be bought by enterprises, and that figure is likely to rise in 2012 and beyond.
entries.metric: share of tablets bought by enterprises
entries.subject: Enterprise tablets

entries.title: eGov: from option to obligation
entries.quote: In 2011 Deloitte predicts e-government (eGov) usage will reach an inflection point. Across developed countries, the proportion of businesses that use eGov services for at least one process is expected to average over 90 percent, up from 75 percent in 2010.
entries.metric: share of businesses in developed countries using eGov for at least one process
entries.subject: E-government

entries.title: Online regulation ratchets up, but cookies live on
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that during the course of 2011 online privacy will provoke more irate headlines and exasperated calls for action than ever before.
entries.subject: Online privacy regulation

entries.title: Squeezing the electrons in: batteries don't follow Moore's Law
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that battery technology will make progress in 2011 and 2012.
entries.subject: Battery technology

entries.title: Hydrogen comes out of hiding: the alternative alternative energy source
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that hydrogen will enjoy tremendous success in 2011.
entries.subject: Hydrogen fuel cells

entries.title: Television's "super media" status strengthens
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2011 television will solidify its status as the current super media, defying some commentators' prophecies of imminent obsolescence.
entries.subject: Television

entries.title: DVRs proliferate! The 30 second spot doesn't die!
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that digital video recorder (DVR) penetration in two large markets will exceed 50 percent of TV households by year-end 2011; but also predicts that TV advertising will be almost entirely unaffected despite that level of penetration.
entries.metric: DVR penetration of TV households in two large markets
entries.subject: Digital video recorders and TV advertising

entries.title: Push beats pull in the battle for the television viewer
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that In 2011 despite the sale of tens of millions of television sets that offer a form of built-in search capability for television programming, the vast majority of viewing will be delivered on a traditional "pushed" basis
entries.subject: Linear (scheduled) TV viewing

entries.title: Social network advertising: how big can it get?
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2011 social networks are likely to surpass the breathtaking milestone of one billion unique members.
entries.subject: Social networks

entries.title: Games go online and on sale: the audience grows, but at what price?
entries.quote: Deloitte forecasts that the total revenue from these relatively new sources could be as high as $10 billion, or 16 percent of total game revenues, by the end of 2012
entries.metric: game revenue from new sources (online, microtransactions)
entries.subject: Video game revenue models
entries.note: 'could be as high as' is an upper bound.

entries.title: Keeping the life in live: A&R diversifies
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2011, the live music sector, with festival organizers at the forefront, will start expanding its talent creation and nurturing role
entries.subject: Live music

entries.title: Pop goes pop-up: music retail goes seasonal and temporary
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that 2011 revenues for digitally distributed music will exceed physical music sales in at least one major market, most likely the United States.
entries.metric: digital music revenue vs physical in at least one major market
entries.subject: Digital music sales

entries.title: Getting to 4G cheaply: will many carriers opt for 3.5G instead?
entries.quote: Deloitte expects that fewer than 30 LTE carriers in six countries will offer commercial service by the end of 2011.
entries.subject: LTE / 4G deployment

entries.title: Wi-Fi complements cellular broadband for "data on the move"
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2011 the volume of data uploaded or downloaded from portable devices via public Wi-Fi networks will grow at a much faster rate (25-50 percent) than the volume carried over cellular broadband networks.
entries.metric: growth of public Wi-Fi data volume from portable devices
entries.subject: Public Wi-Fi data

entries.title: What is "in store" for Wi-Fi: online comparison shopping on aisle 3
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2011, 25 percent of North American big box and anchor tenant retailers will begin offering free in-store Wi-Fi access to shoppers.
entries.metric: share of North American big box retailers offering free in-store Wi-Fi
entries.subject: In-store retail Wi-Fi

entries.title: Video calling: the base goes mainstream, but usage remains niche
entries.quote: Deloitte believes that in 2011 video calling will be cheaper, better and more widely available than ever; yet a boom in demand is unlikely.
entries.subject: Video calling

notes: 10th edition by Deloitte's own count, and the first published as a single TMT report (2002 to 2010 appeared as separate Technology, Media and Telecommunications reports). Rank is the order in the report. Publication month from the launch pattern (January); exact day not confirmed.
